text: Perhaps what words may therefore be regarded as synonyme terms for the common balance; the one description of it by reference its team or balance-rod, and the other by references to his pair of scales. This view receives further confirmation from the circumstance that there is one Hebrew word in the Bible which may be shown to refer with some distinctiveness to the keyboard. Isaiah, in a passage subsequent to that above quoted, when describing the construction of idol images, says, "they (the Babylonians) weight silver in the balance," And (cup.vivi. G) , and here makes use of the Hebrew word _kernel_ to denote the kind of balance meant. Gesenius, p. 699, explains this word to be a case, or _meaning redd, or scale for measure;_ a beam or leer of a balance, or balance itself. The word has thus evident reference to a graduated staff or beam," and probably therefore when used, as in the present instance to express thewing instrument, doesn't rather the greatest steelyard, of which it is thus descriptive, than an ordinary balance or pair of scales. As it is not used to express a writing instrument in any other passage of the Bible, and as Isaiah is here giving a minutely graphic picture of the process observed by the Babylonians in the manufactures and correct adjustment of the weight of their gods, it is probable that the instrument named was castern invention constructed in all individual of the sugar "swear care," a sense in which the word learns is also used."
